bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to civil commitment; establishing a process to vacate an order any time based on error or false information; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 253B.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[+[253B.30] POST CIVIL COMMITMENT RELIEF. +]

[+(a) An aggrieved party subject to a court order issued under this chapter on or after January 1, 2015, may file a petition at any time to vacate the order if the order was issued in error or relied on false or erroneous information. The court must grant the petition and vacate the order if the petitioner demonstrates by a preponderance of the evidence that the order was issued in error or relied on false or erroneous information. +]

[+(b) An aggrieved party may appeal an order issued under this section as in other civil cases by filing an appeal at any time after an order is issued under this section. +]

[+EFFECTIVE DATE.+]

[+This section is effective August 1, 2026. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to civil commitment; establishing a process to vacate an order any time based on error or false information; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 253B.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[253B.30] POST CIVIL COMMITMENT RELIEF.

(a) An aggrieved party subject to a court order issued under this chapter on or after January 1, 2015, may file a petition at any time to vacate the order if the order was issued in error or relied on false or erroneous information. The court must grant the petition and vacate the order if the petitioner demonstrates by a preponderance of the evidence that the order was issued in error or relied on false or erroneous information.

(b) An aggrieved party may appeal an order issued under this section as in other civil cases by filing an appeal at any time after an order is issued under this section.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective August 1, 2026.
additions: (a) An aggrieved party subject to a court order issued under this chapter on or after January 1, 2015, may file a petition at any time to vacate the order if the order was issued in error or relied on false or erroneous information. The court must grant the petition and vacate the order if the petitioner demonstrates by a preponderance of the evidence that the order was issued in error or relied on false or erroneous information.
(b) An aggrieved party may appeal an order issued under this section as in other civil cases by filing an appeal at any time after an order is issued under this section.
